content:
Talia Benson: Now that the streaming/tool-calling/structured-output refresh is live, can we align on post-launch monitoring for the next ~2 weeks? Want to catch regressions fast + make sure we actually see support load go down.

Proposed (pls react/adjust):
1) Support ticket trend checks (daily for 1 week, then 2x/week)
2) Docs analytics (pageviews + code copy + search queries)
3) Follow-up patch plan + owners if we see issues (SDK/doc/examples)

Connor O'Brien: +1. For releases, I’d like us to explicitly watch SDK version adoption too (are users staying on older versions w/ old snippets?). I can pull npm/pypi/go module download deltas + the changelog clickthrough.

Priya Shah: Support side: I can track new tickets w/ tags we’ve been using: `streaming`, `tool-calling`, `structured-output`, and the internal “examples-refresh” label.
Baseline from last 14 days pre-launch:
- ~11 tickets/week streaming disconnect/assembly confusion
- ~7 tickets/week tool args partial/truncated / "tool result shape" questions
- ~5 tickets/week JSON parse / "schema" confusion
Main ones we referenced in the writeup: SUP-18421, SUP-18436, SUP-18452.

Dev Patel: Also want to watch for *misleading success* tickets: “it works but is slow / weird output” because of fallback behavior. We’ve seen folks accidentally disable streaming / parse incremental JSON incorrectly and then blame latency.
If we add a canned macro linking to the updated docs + runnable example, that should reduce back-and-forth. I can draft.

Ibrahim Khan: For engineering signals, we can use the counters from the monorepo smoke tests + any telemetry we already added:
- `stream_disconnect`
- `tool_call_partial_args`
- `final_message_assembly_mismatch`
- `structured_output_validation_fail`
We should set a simple threshold doc: if `structured_output_validation_fail` spikes after a release, we patch examples first (usually parsing/validation guidance), then SDK if needed.

Monica Patel: Agree. For SDKs, I’d like to keep a small "patch runway" open for 1–2 weeks. If we see confusion that’s clearly caused by a footgun in sample code (esp TS types), I’d rather cut a patch version quickly than let it sit.
Proposed escalation path:
- docs-only fix -> PR in redwood-docs same day
- SDK example fix (no API change) -> patch release within 48h
- semantics ambiguity -> route to Brian for signoff, then decide

Elliot Price: Docs analytics: Wei and I can watch the streaming + tool calling + structured output pages.
Metrics we can track in GA:
- pageviews + unique users
- avg time on page (spike can indicate confusion)
- outbound clicks to GitHub runnable examples
- code block “copy” events by language tab
Also: top internal search queries on docs for “tool_call”, “json mode”, “schema”, “stream disconnect”.

Wei Chen: I’ll add a quick dashboard view for the 3 updated guides + the quickstart README pages. We should also monitor 404s from the redirects we pushed (there was a lot of renaming). If 404s show up, I can update redirects.

Sahana Iyer: CI side: I’ll keep an eye on the snippet-sync job (from the monorepo check). If we start shipping patch doc changes quickly, we’ll likely trip it.
Action item: if you see a snippet-sync failure, don’t "fix" by turning it off — ping me/Leila and we’ll update fixtures or relax the check (within reason).

Leila Farouk: +1. Also: golden transcript tests for streaming tool-calls can flake if model output drifts. We should treat those as "contract tests" for event shape, not content.
If we see flakes:
- first step: confirm event ordering + required fields still match
- if content drift: update fixtures and pin model version used by tests
- if ordering drift: that’s a real regression

Renee Sullivan: From DevRel side, I can monitor community inbound (help channel / Discord) for the same confusion patterns. If we see repeated Qs, I’ll propose a short “Known pitfalls” snippet we can paste into responses + link to docs.

Talia Benson: Great. Let’s lock a lightweight cadence + owners.

Cadence (next 10 business days):
- Daily (Mon–Fri): Support trend quick check (Priya/Dev)
- Mon/Wed/Fri: Docs analytics + 404s (Wei/Elliot)
- Tue/Thu: SDK adoption + release notes clickthrough (Connor)
- 2x/week: CI/golden test health pass (Sahana/Leila)

Escalation / patch plan:
- P0 (broken snippet / copy-paste fails): same-day docs PR + patch SDK if needed
- P1 (confusing but works): docs clarification within 48h, add to known pitfalls
- P2 (nice-to-have): batch into next minor release

Can folks confirm what “P0” looks like from your side?

Dev Patel: P0 for Support = any ticket where customer is blocked in prod and it’s directly linked to our example showing the wrong loop/message shape. Also if there’s a pattern >3 tickets/day w/ same symptom.
Examples:
- "TS tool result shape mismatch" (like SUP-18452) would be P0 if it resurfaces
- “structured output example produces invalid JSON” would be P0 (even if model is at fault, we need safe handling + retries documented)

Priya Shah: +1. I’ll post a daily note in this thread (or a new one?) with counts + any notable new tickets.
Format:
- new tickets (count)
- top issue label
- links
- suggested fix (docs/sdk)

Ibrahim Khan: For P0/P1 guidelines on streaming JSON:
- If users are parsing partial deltas as JSON (common), that’s on us to make the example scream "only parse after final".
- If final assembly is wrong (we drop a chunk / tool args truncated), that’s SDK/example bug -> P0.
Also we should keep pointing to the workaround for partial tool args: accumulate `arguments_delta` until `tool_call.completed` (or whatever we named it in the conventions), then parse.

Monica Patel: For SDK patch releases, I can coordinate with Dana (TS) + Mateusz (Go) as needed, but please funnel through Ibrahim to avoid three different fixes.

Wei Chen: For docs P0: broken code tabs / copy button issues also count (we had that INT-3321 thing before). If the UI regresses, that’s immediately a P0 because it amplifies everything.

Connor O'Brien: I’ll start a small tracker doc (just a bulleted log) for "post-launch issues + action taken" so we can include it in the retro + release notes if needed.

Sahana Iyer: One more thing: if we do patch releases quickly, can we keep model versions in examples pinned? Otherwise smoke tests can pass locally then fail in CI due to default model drift.

Leila Farouk: +1. We should explicitly pin:
- model name + version (if supported)
- and in docs call out “if you’re using a different model family, structured output guarantees may vary.”

Talia Benson: Ok. Action items:
- Priya: start daily support trend posts tomorrow EOD
- Wei/Elliot: share docs analytics links here once dashboards are ready
- Connor: share adoption + clickthrough summary by Thu
- Sahana/Leila: write a short "what to do when golden tests flake" snippet we can paste into PRs
- Ibrahim: draft a 1-pager of P0 vs P1 criteria + escalation owner map

(reactions: :thumbsup: 6)

Priya Shah: Works. I’ll also add a note if I see the old outdated snippet quoted in tickets — that’s a good signal we need better SEO / redirects.

Elliot Price: Dashboards should be up in a couple hours. Will drop links + initial read (esp code-copy by language; we can see if Go users are actually using the new helper).

Monica Patel: Thanks all. Please tag me only if it’s P0 (I’m trying to keep patch bandwidth focused). Otherwise tag Ibrahim + the relevant owner.

Talia Benson: Closing the loop: let’s keep this thread as the running log for the first week, then we can roll it into a short retro note + decide if monitoring cadence relaxes.
